title: Mind the Gap: Structure-Aware Consistency in Preference Learning
claim: A fixed margin over-constrains near-equivalent items and causes violations; an adaptive margin relaxes for similar pairs while staying strict for distinct ones.
layout: 2 side-by-side panels, left-to-right, shared axes with red vs green callouts
description: Two side-by-side scatter-style panels share a 'Score Space (h)' x-axis. The left panel is titled 'Uniform Margin (Standard DPO)'. It shows a diagonal black decision boundary inside a constant-width gray band bounded by dashed gray lines. A red-outlined 'Margin Violation!' callout has an arrow pointing to a red triangle (loser) and a blue circle (winner) that lie close together inside the band. The right panel is titled 'Structure-Aware (Ours / SA-DPO)'. It has the same diagonal boundary, but the band is green and varies in width: it pinches to almost nothing at the close pair and widens away from it. A green 'Margin Relaxes' callout points to that pinch point. A legend at the bottom explains the zones, winner and loser markers, and the decision boundary. The red and green contrast draws the eye first.
caption: Uniform vs. Structure-Aware Margins. (Left) A fixed margin γ forces artificial separation on semantically similar pairs (synonyms), causing hallucination. (Right) SA-DPO scales the margin by semantic distance ∆(y, y′), relaxing constraints for synonyms while enforcing strict separation on distinct pairs.
abstract: Aligning Large Language Models (LLMs) with human intent, whether through explicit reward modeling or direct methods such as DPO, fundamentally relies on minimizing a surrogate loss as a proxy for the true pairwise ranking objective. We prove that this reliance is flawed for the standard surrogate losses used: for the equicontinuous hypothesis sets characteristic of neural networks, no standard surrogate provides a meaningful consistency guarantee. Minimizing the surrogate loss to zero can leave the true ranking error arbitrarily high. To resolve this, we formulate LLM alignment within a margin-shifted ranking framework and derive $H$-consistency bounds showing that enforcing a confidence margin $Î³$ is not merely beneficial but necessary for consistency. We further introduce Structure-Aware $H$-consistency and a corresponding objective (SA-DPO) that adapts the margin to the semantic distance between responses, preventing instability on near-synonymous pairs. Finally, we analyze the trade-off between the margin required for consistency and the model's finite capacity to satisfy it, revealing a strict hierarchy of surrogate losses: heavy-tailed surrogates (e.g., the Polynomial Hinge family) offer strictly superior consistency guarantees for capacity-bounded models compared to the logistic loss used in DPO. Experiments on UltraFeedback and Argilla DPO-Mix-7k confirm that SA-DPO consistently outperforms DPO and SimPO, with a 58.5% head-to-head win-rate in downstream generation quality.
